question: Which selector and which property does the panel stylesheet declare a value for, what value does it declare as text, and what value does the panel render today — and which of those values could not be resolved without a browser?

capture.writes: one: the armed test re-derives this record from the files below and writes it only when a value moved, and it refuses to write a candidate that is not a fixed point of this suite’s default pin
capture.note: the instant this record was first written; every re-capture derives through it, so the record moves for no clock - the values it carries are read from the stylesheet and the document at every run, and none of them is a time

sources.contributes: the declarations themselves: every rule, its media context, its selector as authored and the value text it carries, read from the file rather than from a normalised copy of it.

the document the computed readings are taken from and the hooks the style suite measures it on: this suite imports `panelMarkup`, `documentWith`, `darkBlock`, `measure`, `MEASURED_HOOKS`, `DARK_HOOKS`, `MEASURED_PROPERTIES` and `STATES` from it, so the surface recorded here is that suite’s surface and not a second one.

facts.media: The media context the declaration sits in: `all` for the sheet’s own rules, and the dark block’s own media text for the rules it carries, so a value the dark scheme restates is recorded beside the value it restates rather than instead of it.
facts.selector: The selector the value is declared under, exactly as the stylesheet authors it — a selector list keeps its own line breaks and its own quote characters, so the record names the declaration a reader can find in the file and never a normalised spelling of it.
facts.selectorParts: The same selector split into the parts a document can be asked for, so every part of a selector list is either the element the reading was taken from or a part recorded as rendered by nothing in the measured document.
facts.document: The document the computed reading was taken from: the default markup `scripts/panel-styles.test.mjs` renders, a document carrying that suite’s own state value where the selector names one of the four states, or the default document with the dark block’s rules appended as a second sheet — which is how that suite measures the scheme, since jsdom implements no `matchMedia`.
facts.property: The CSS property as the stylesheet authors it, shorthands included: `border-top` is recorded as `border-top` and not as the longhands it expands to, so the row names the declaration the author wrote.
facts.declared: The value the stylesheet declares, as the text its author wrote: hex colours, `currentcolor`, `inherit` and shorthands are carried unexpanded and unnormalised, because a normalised value could not tell the token layer re-expressing this value from the token layer retuning it.
facts.computed: The value `window.getComputedStyle` resolves for that declaration on the element the measured document renders, read through `scripts/panel-styles.test.mjs`’s own `documentWith` and `panelMarkup` — or, where the value cannot be resolved without a browser, a named absence carrying the measurement that showed it unread rather than a value only jsdom would agree with.
